title: Pin Payment Handler to Payment Nodes
description:
**SITUATION:**

Payment Handler is already running (**2** replicas), but nothing steers where those Pods land. The scheduler places them **wherever there is capacity** — so across a multi-node cluster they can end up on any worker (payments, notifications, general). That is fine for many apps; it is **not** fine for Payment Handler.

**Why a payment pool?** QuickByte handles card charges. Compliance and ops treat some workers as the **payment / PCI pool** (**PCI** = Payment Card Industry rules for card data). Those machines get tighter reviews and dedicated networking. Payment Handler should run **only there** — not on notification or general nodes.

Platform already labeled that pool `workload=payments`. Your job is to teach the Deployment that **hard** rule so replicas stop landing at random on other pools.

This lab introduces a hard **`nodeSelector`** (Pods choose the pool). Soft preferences come next; **taints** that keep *other* apps *off* PCI machines come in a later lab.
[DevSetu Blog — Where Pods Land: Selectors, Affinity, and Taints](/play/devops-engineer/kubernetes/read/scheduling-affinity-taints)

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Discover which nodes are in the payment pool (`kubectl get nodes --show-labels`) and where the Pods are today (`kubectl get pods -o wide`).
2. **Update** the Payment Handler Deployment so Pods use a **`nodeSelector`** for that pool.
3. Verify Pods are **Ready** and running **only** on payment-labeled nodes.

**SPEC:**

- Deployment name: `payment-handler` (do not rename)
- Replicas: keep **`2`**
- `nodeSelector`: `workload: payments`
- Keep existing container image, labels, and port
- Ready: **2/2** Pods Ready on nodes labeled `workload=payments`

**GOOD PRACTICES:**

- Manifest: `payment-handler-nodeselector-l25.yaml`.
- Do **not** use nodeAffinity / taints for this lab — plain `nodeSelector` only.
- Work only in your lab namespace (not `default`).

hints: Your namespace is in the lab chrome and in $LEARNER_NS — kubectl already defaults there.
Payment / PCI pool nodes are labeled workload=payments — pin with nodeSelector only in this lab.
Check kubectl get nodes --show-labels and kubectl get pods -l app=payment-handler -o wide before and after.
Work only in your lab namespace (not default).
Read SPEC carefully, apply your YAML, then Submit.

problemStatement.solution:
# Solution — Pin Payment Handler to Payment Nodes

Pin Payment Handler to the **payment / PCI pool** (Payment Card Industry–scoped workers) with a hard `nodeSelector` so replicas only land on nodes labeled `workload=payments`.

Docs: [DevSetu Blog — Where Pods Land: Selectors, Affinity, and Taints](/play/devops-engineer/kubernetes/read/scheduling-affinity-taints) · [Assigning Pods to Nodes](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node/)

## Solution YAML

Save as `payment-handler-nodeselector-l25.yaml`:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payment-handler
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payment-handler
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: payment-handler
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        workload: payments
      containers:
        - name: payment-handler
          image: devsetu/payment-handler:v1.0
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8000
```

## Declarative

```bash
kubectl apply -f payment-handler-nodeselector-l25.yaml
kubectl get deploy payment-handler -o wide
kubectl get pods -l app=payment-handler -o wide
```

Wait until **2/2** Pods are Ready on payment-labeled nodes, then **Submit**. Use `nodeSelector` only (no affinity/taints).
